# Results — Study 756 (Challenger-Layoffs)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The macro-nowcasting
folklore — **a spike in announced job cuts warns you the market is about to weaken** —
tested on the monthly **Challenger, Gray & Christmas** job-cut tape (a hardcoded,
clearly-labelled **approximate** snapshot, since Challenger's series is proprietary with
no free feed) against month-end **SPY** (yfinance, total-return adjusted). We split forward
1/3/6/12-month SPY returns into months when job cuts are **spiking** vs **calm**, compare
each to the unconditional base rate, and add a Welch *t*, a Newey-West **HAC** *t*, a
placebo null, a lead/lag scan and a tradable timing overlay. Offline & deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Job-cut tape | **Challenger, Gray & Christmas** monthly announced job cuts (thousands); **hardcoded, labelled, *approximate* snapshot** of the public press-release headlines |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Window | 2000-01-31 → 2026-06-30 (**318** months; **26.4** years) |
| Signal | cut spike = month above its **trailing-12-month** average (excess > 0); **SPIKE** fires in **41%** of months |
| Entry / costs | **1-month execution lag** (the report for month *t* is released early in *t+1*; act on the next month-end close); 10 bps one-way per switch on the overlay |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** Challenger's series is proprietary and
> has no free FRED/yfinance feed, so the job-cut tape is a hardcoded **approximate
> reconstruction** from Challenger's published monthly headline totals — public and
> faithful in shape, but **not the exact revised vintage**. The famous **COVID-2020
> spike** (the record **~671k** announced cuts in **April 2020**) is included faithfully
> and, being one enormous coincident shock, dominates any cuts-vs-returns association — a
> fact the verdict leans on, not around.

## The signal — forward SPY returns when job cuts SPIKE vs the base rate

1-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say a SPIKE should
depress the forward return; Welch *t* compares the SPIKE-set mean to the unconditional
mean, and the **HAC *t*** is the spike-dummy coefficient with Newey-West errors (lag =
horizon, to correct the overlapping forward windows). A real early-warning ⇒ **significantly
negative** *t*. The placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size month draws whose
mean forward return is **at most** the SPIKE set's.

| horizon | n spike | spike mean | calm mean | base mean | spike down-rate | base down-rate | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1-month**  | 131 | **+0.25%** | +1.16% | +0.78% | 44% | 36% | **−1.05** | **−1.66** | 0.081 |
| 3-month  | 131 | **+1.70%** | +2.75% | +2.31% | 33% | 31% | −0.73 | −0.85 | 0.174 |
| 6-month  | 131 | **+3.54%** | +5.50% | +4.67% | 33% | 27% | −0.88 | −0.98 | 0.120 |
| 12-month | 130 | **+8.57%** | +10.63% | +9.75% | 25% | 22% | −0.58 | −0.61 | 0.211 |

Read it carefully. The **direction matches the folklore** at every horizon: after a job-cut
spike, forward SPY returns are **lower** than the base rate and the market is *down* more
often. The strongest effect is the **announcement-drift** month right after the print
(**+0.25% vs +0.78%**, down-rate **44% vs 36%**, HAC *t* = **−1.66**, placebo *p* = **0.08**)
— but even that **fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar**, and it *fades* as the horizon lengthens. The right
sign, inside the noise.

## The decisive test — does the cut spike *lead* the market?

The whole pitch is **"early."** So we scan the correlation of the cut-spike signal at *t*
against the SPY return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine early-warning would show its strongest
*negative* correlation at a **positive** lead (cuts move first, the market falls later).

| lead *L* (months) | −3 | −2 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(cut-spike, fwd SPY) | **−0.24** | **−0.25** | −0.05 | +0.02 | +0.02 | +0.08 | +0.09 |

The strongest negative correlation sits at **L = −2** — the cut spike is most associated
with a market move *two months in its **past***. At positive leads (cuts supposedly leading)
the correlation is near **zero or positive**. Announced cuts aren't an early-warning; the
spike is a **coincident-to-lagging** echo of a market that already turned. That is the core
of the "early-warning? — Not supported" stamp.

## Tradability — the "go to cash when cuts spike" overlay

Hold SPY when cuts are calm, sit in cash when they spike (one-month lag; 10 bps per switch,
turnover one-way × NAV). Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns 0 here — a
conservative, labelled simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold SPY | **+9.3%** | **0.61** | — |
| overlay, gross | +5.7% | 0.55 | 102 |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+5.3%** | **0.51** | 102 |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** on both return (**+5.3% vs +9.3%** net) and
Sharpe (**0.51 vs 0.61**). Sitting out the market whenever cuts spike forfeits return
without buying enough downside protection to pay for it — even *before* costs. The signal
isn't merely un-extractable; acting on it **loses money relative to doing nothing.**

## Robustness — window, threshold, and the COVID dependence

| variation | n spike | spike 12m mean | base 12m mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| trailing window **w = 6** | 139 | +7.4% | +9.8% | −1.25 | −1.56 | 0.049 |
| trailing window **w = 12** (base) | 130 | +8.6% | +9.8% | −0.58 | −0.61 | 0.211 |
| trailing window **w = 24** | 121 | +9.5% | +9.8% | −0.14 | −0.11 | 0.421 |
| threshold **> +50%** | 34 | +13.5% | +9.8% | **+0.98** | +0.67 | 0.908 |
| **drop 2020–2021** (ex-COVID), 12m | 121 | +8.7% | +10.7% | −0.89 | −1.03 | 0.116 |

Two lessons. (1) The effect *strengthens with a shorter trailing window* (w = 6 → HAC
*t* = −1.56) and at the **1-month** horizon (HAC *t* = −1.66) — the announcement-drift
signature — but still never clears the bar. (2) Push the threshold to a **big** cut spike
(> +50% over trend) and the sign **flips positive** (Welch *t* = +0.98): the largest spikes
are recession *bottoms* you'd want to be buying, not selling. And dropping the COVID years
leaves the 12-month *t* at **−0.89**. No specification clears *t* = 2.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly job-cut + SPY-like series with a *planted* link (a cut spike at *t*
depresses the *t+1* return by `edge`). The detector + inference must recover a planted edge
and must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n spike | spike 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 119 | +0.44% | +0.66% | **−0.53** | −0.76 | 0.277 |
| **+0.04** (large link) | 119 | −2.87% | −0.65% | **−5.44** | **−7.84** | 0.001 |

With **no** planted link the test sits at *t* = −0.53 (no false positive); a large planted
link drives the HAC *t* to **−7.84**. The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape HAC *t*
of ~−1.7 (at its strongest) is exactly what an *absent-or-tiny* cuts→returns edge looks like
through this keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The folklore's **direction is real** — a job-cut spike precedes
  modestly lower, more-often-negative forward returns at every horizon, sharpest in the
  **announcement-drift month** (spike +0.25% vs base +0.78%, HAC *t* = −1.66, placebo
  *p* = 0.08) — but the excess **fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar** at every horizon and spec, is
  fragile to the trailing window, and **flips sign** for the biggest spikes. Real-as-lore,
  weak-as-edge; the Challenger tape is a labelled *proxy*, so magnitude is a proxy result too.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "cash when cuts spike" overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold**
  gross *and* net (**+5.3% vs +9.3%**, Sharpe **0.51 vs 0.61**). The signal doesn't just fail
  to add value — acting on it **destroys** return. Nothing to allocate to.
- **Early warning? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan puts the strongest *negative*
  correlation at **L = −2** (the cut spike *lagging* the market by two months); at positive
  leads it's ~zero. Announced cuts are a **coincident-to-lagging** echo, not a leader. The
  whole appeal — *early* — is the part the data rejects.
